title: Font tier edge rules: a longer negative shifts one tier smaller (clamped at 8px); a document with no positive dollar value stays at 11px
permissions_required: A user with Reports access who can open the Sales By Representative report.
preconditions: 1. You can produce a view where a negative value's parenthesized rendering is LONGER than the largest positive value, and (separately) a view with no positive dollar value at all (for example, the empty export or an all-negative result).
steps: 1. Download a PDF for the view whose longest value is a parenthesized negative longer than any positive; note the body size against the positive value's own tier.
2. Download a PDF for a view with zero matching invoices (or all-negative values); note the body size.
expected: 1. When a negative's parenthesized rendering is longer than the largest positive, the base tier shifts ONE step smaller than the positive value's tier, clamped at the 8px floor (already-8px stays 8px).
2. With no positive dollar value in the document, the base tier is the 11px ceiling and the negative shift does not apply — the tier stays 11px.
3. In all cases the fixed column widths prevent overflow.
